title: Scott Trust Limited
wikitext:
{{Short description|British multinational mass media company}} {{Use British English|date=June 2016}} {{Use dmy dates|date=July 2026}} The '''Scott Trust Limited''' is the British [[limited company]] that owns [[Guardian Media Group]] and thus ''[[The Guardian]]'' as well as various other media businesses in the UK. It was created as a [[Trust (law)|trust]] to acquire ''The Guardian'' in 1936, and reorganised as a limited company in 2008. The company is responsible for appointing the editor of ''The Guardian'' (and those of the group's other main newspapers) but, apart from enjoining them to continue the paper's editorial policy on "the same lines and in the same spirit as heretofore", it has a policy of not interfering in their decisions. The arrangement tends to give editors a long tenure: for example, the last incumbent, [[Alan Rusbridger]], held the position from 1995 until 2015. The current chairman of the Scott Trust Board is Ole Jacob Sunde,{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2016/sep/22/alex-graham-appointed-chair-scott-trust-guardian-media-group|title=Alex Graham appointed as seventh chair of the Scott Trust|last=Jackson|first=Jasper|date=2016-09-22|work=The Guardian|access-date=2017-02-28|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}} who replaced [[Alex Graham (producer)|Alex Graham]] in 2021. Others on the eleven-member board include the current editor-in-chief [[Katharine Viner]], Guardian legal affairs correspondent Haroon Siddique who is the journalist director of the board, and one member of the Scott family.{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/the-scott-trust/2015/jul/26/the-scott-trust-board|title=The Scott Trust board|date=2015-07-26|work=The Guardian|access-date=2017-02-28|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}} The Scott Trust is a limited partner in GMG Ventures LP, founded in 2017,{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/gmg/2018/jul/24/about-guardian-media-group|title=About Guardian Media Group|date=24 Jul 2018|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=2020-06-25}} according to the GMG 2018 annual report, "this £42m venture capital fund is designed to contribute financial returns and to support GMG’s strategy by investing in early stage businesses focused on developing the next generation of media technology".{{cite news |title=Guardian Media Group plc (GMG) results for the financial year ended 1 April 2018 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/gnm-press-office/2018/jul/24/guardian-media-group-plc-gmg-results-for-the-financial-year-ended-1-april-2018 |work=The Guardian |date=24 July 2018}} == History == === 1936–1948 === [[File:John Russell Scott, oil painting by Francis Dodd.jpg|thumb|[[John Russell Scott]] by [[Francis Dodd (artist)|Francis Dodd]]]] The Trust was established in 1936 by [[John Russell Scott]], owner of the ''Manchester Guardian'' (as it then was) and the ''[[Manchester Evening News]]''. After the deaths in quick succession of his father [[C. P. Scott]] and brother [[Edward Taylor Scott|Edward]], and consequent threat of [[Inheritance Tax (United Kingdom)|death duties]], John Scott wished to prevent future [[Inheritance tax|death duties]] forcing the closure or sale of the newspapers, and to protect the liberal editorial line of the ''Guardian'' from interference by future proprietors. The first and only chairman of the first Trust was John Scott. === 1948–2008 === The Trust was dissolved and reformed in 1948, as it was thought that the Trust, under the terms of the original trust deed, had become liable to tax due to changes in the law. At this time John Scott also gave up his exclusive right to appoint [[trustee]]s; the trustees would henceforth appoint new members themselves. Five months after the signing of the new trust deed, John Scott died. After three years of legal argument, the [[Inland Revenue]] gave up its claim for death duty. The eight initial trustees of the 1948 Trust were all connected with the Manchester Guardian and Evening News, Ltd., and included four of C. P. Scott's grandsons as well as the then editor of ''The Guardian'', [[A. P. Wadsworth]]. It has become normal practice for a ''Guardian'' journalist to be a member of the trust, though they are not considered to be a "representative" of the staff, as this may result in a conflict of interests. In 1992, the Trust identified its central objective: :"To secure the financial and editorial independence of ''The Guardian'' in perpetuity: as a quality national newspaper without party affiliation; remaining faithful to its liberal tradition; as a profit-seeking enterprise managed in an efficient and cost-effective manner." The Trust saw its main functions as being the following: * "To secure the Trust's own continuity by renewing its membership and by dealing with threats to its existence * To monitor the organisation, financial management and overall strategy of the Group, holding the Board accountable for its performance * To appoint and 'in extreme circumstances' to dismiss the editors of ''The Guardian'', the ''Manchester Evening News'' (and ''The Observer'' after its acquisition in 1993) * To act as a 'court of appeal' in the event of any dispute between the editorial and managerial sides of the operation."{{cite book |last=Ellis |first=Gavin |date=2014 |title=Trust Ownership and the Future of News: Media Moguls and White Knights |location=London |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan |pages=157–58 |isbn=9781137369437 }} The second Trust had five Chairmen over its 60 years: [[Alfred Powell Wadsworth]] (1948–56), [[Richard Farquhar Scott]] (1956–84), [[Alastair Hetherington]] (1984–89), [[Hugo Young]] (1990–2003) and [[Liz Forgan]] (2003–2008). === The Scott Trust Limited: 2008–present === In October 2008, it was announced that the trust was being wound up and its assets transferred to a new limited company named "The Scott Trust Limited" to ''strengthen the protection it offers to the Guardian'' and because ''[l]ike all non-charitable trusts, and unlike limited companies, the Scott Trust has a finite lifespan''.{{cite web | url=https://www.theguardian.com/gnm-press-office/scott-trust-updates-structure | title=Scott Trust updates structure | date=2008-10-08 | work=The Guardian | access-date=2019-07-29}} The core purpose of the Trust was enshrined in the constitution of the limited company and "cannot be altered or amended." The new company is barred from paying dividends, and "its constitution has been carefully drafted to ensure that no individual can ever personally benefit from the arrangements."{{cite web|url=https://www.pressgazette.co.uk/guardian-owning-scott-trust-to-fold-after-72-years/|title=Guardian-owning Scott Trust to fold after 72 years|author=Dominic Ponsford|date=2008-10-08|publisher=[[Press Gazette]]}} In February 2010, the company announced the sale of its GMG Regional Media arm and its regional print titles to the [[Trinity Mirror|Trinity Mirror Group]]. The regional titles comprised the ''[[Manchester Evening News]]'' and 31 others in the North West and South of England. The sale was finalised on 28 March 2010 and ended the Scott Trust's association with regional newspapers. In 2012 the Scott Trust Limited became a co-founder of the [[European Press Prize]].{{Cite web|title=Members|url=https://www.europeanpressprize.com/foundation/members/|access-date=2021-08-23|website=European Press Prize}} Guardian News and Media, a subsidiary of the Scott Trust Limited, reported a loss of £30.9 million for the year to the end of April 2013. The company via the Guardian Media Group (GMG, a subsidiary company) completed the sale for £619 million of its 50.1% stake in ''[[Auto Trader Group|Auto Trader]]'' on 4 March 2014. [[Apax Partners]], a venture capital firm, increased its share to become the sole shareholder in the business. The £619 million earned from the sale of ''Auto Trader'' added to the £253.7 million of cash and investments which GMG published in its 2013 annual report. This left an investment fund which was likely to be in excess of £850 million to underwrite ''Guardian'' losses.{{cite web | url=https://www.pressgazette.co.uk/guardian-secure-for-generations-to-come-after-tax-free-bonanza-of-619m-from-auto-trader-sale/ | title=Guardian 'secure for generations to come' after tax-free bonanza of £619 million from Auto Trader sale | date=2014-03-04 | publisher=Press Gazette | access-date=2019-07-29}} In December 2014, it was announced that [[Alan Rusbridger]], then ''Guardian'' editor-in-chief, would succeed Forgan as the chairman of the company in 2016{{cite web | url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2014/dec/10/alan-rusbridger-stand-down-guardian-editor-in-chief | title=Alan Rusbridger to stand down as Guardian editor-in-chief | author=Jane Martinson | date=2014-12-10 | work=The Guardian | access-date=2019-07-29}} but he unexpectedly announced on 13 May 2016 his resignation as a director.{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-36287551 | title=Former Guardian editor Alan Rusbridger leaves Scott Trust | date=2016-05-13 | publisher=[[BBC News]] | access-date=2019-07-29}} As of January 2016, the company's funds were £740 million, down from £838.3 million in July 2015.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2016/mar/17/guardian-media-group-to-cut-250-jobs|title=Guardian Media Group to cut 250 jobs in bid to break even within three years|first=Jane|last=Martinson|date=17 March 2016|work=The Guardian}} As of 1 April 2018, the value of the Scott Trust Endowment Fund was £1.01 billion, down slightly from £1.03 billion in 2017. In 2023, following independent academic research commissioned in 2020 reporting, the trust apologised for the newspaper's founders' involvement in [[Slavery in Britain|transatlantic slavery]] principally through the cotton trade. It announced a £10 million ten-year programme of [[restorative justice]].{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2023/mar/28/guardian-owner-apologises-founders-transatlantic-slavery-scott-trust |title=Guardian owner apologises for founders' links to transatlantic slavery |last=Mohdin |first=Aamna |newspaper=The Guardian |date=28 March 2023 |access-date=28 March 2023}} In November 2024, Jonathan Paine was appointed to the board of the Scott Trust. Paine is a former managing director and senior adviser at Rothschild & Co.{{Cite news |last=Warrington |first=James |date=2024-11-13 |title=Guardian owner appoints former Rothschild banker to board amid Observer sale |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2024/11/13/guardian-owner-appoints-ex-rothschild-banker-board-observer/ |access-date=2024-11-13 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235}} In early December 2024, the company announced the sale of ''[[The Observer]]'' to Tortoise Media.{{cite web |title=Observer Sold |url=https://pressgazette.co.uk/publishers/nationals/observer-sold-tortoise-media/ |access-date=20 December 2024}} Two weeks later the company confirmed the deal, and that it had taken a stock position in the purchaser.{{Cite news |date=2024-12-18|last1=Thomas |first1=Daniel |title=Tortoise Media closes deal to buy Observer |url=https://on.ft.com/3DgD4sA |access-date=2024-12-27 |work=[[Financial Times]]}}{{cite web |last1=Pylas |first1=Pan |date=18 December 2024 |title=World's oldest Sunday newspaper, the UK's Observer, sold in face of journalistic opposition |url=https://apnews.com/britain-newspaper-guardian-observer-tortoise-media |publisher=[[The Associated Press]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241218152203/https://apnews.com/britain-newspaper-guardian-observer-tortoise-media |archive-date=18 December 2024 }} == Governance == Scott Trust Limited was incorporated on 24 September 2008 as ''Scott Place 1001 Limited'', and adopted its current name on 3 October 2008; its number is 06706464 and it is a [[Private company limited by shares|company limited by shares]].{{cite web | url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/06706464 | title=Company overview for the Scott Trust Limited on Companies House website | publisher=[[Companies House]] | access-date=2021-03-29}} The Scott Trust Limited is governed according to the [[articles of association]], set up in 2008 and filed at [[Companies House]].{{cite web | url=https://uploads.guim.co.uk/2018/07/24/1.4_STL_corporate_governance_2018.pdf | title=THE SCOTT TRUST LIMITED: Corporate governance | date=2018-07-23 | work=[[The Guardian]] | access-date=2019-08-05}} The articles say that the [[board of directors]] must guard editorial independence. The board appoints itself under article 63, through an appointments committee. Neither workers at the newspapers nor readers participate in voting for board members. Such voting could be allowed with 75% approval of the existing board of directors under article 7.{{citation needed|date=April 2020}} == The Scott Trust Board == === Current members === {| class="wikitable" !Name !Joined !Position |- |Ole Jacob Sunde |2015 |Chairman of the Scott Trust Limited board (2021–present) |- |[[Katharine Viner]] |June 2015 |Editor-in-chief, Guardian News and Media (June 2015 – present) |- |Tracy Corrigan |2022 | |- |Margaret Simons |2022 | |- |[[David Olusoga]] |June 2018 |Historian, had also been writing for ''The Guardian'' |- |Russell Scott |2015 |Senior Independent Director |- |[[Haroon Siddique]] |2022 |Journalist director of the Scott Trust Limited board (2022 – present) |- |Matthew Ryder |2020 | |- |[[Nabiha Syed]] |2023 | |- |Jonathan Paine |2024 | |- |Jane Martinson |2025 | |- |Sam Gregory |2025 | |-{{cite web|url=https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/company/06706464/filing-history|title=THE SCOTT TRUST LIMITED - Filing history|publisher=[[Companies House]]}} |} === Past members === {| class="wikitable" !Name !Position |- |[[Alex Graham (producer)|Alex Graham]] |Chair of the Scott Trust Limited (2016 – 2021) |- |[[Liz Forgan]] |Chair of the Scott Trust (2003 – 2008)
Chair of Scott Trust Limited (2008 – 2016) |- |[[Hugo Young]] |Chair of the Scott Trust (1989 – 2003) |- |Alistair Hetherington |Chair of the Scott Trust (1984 – 1989) |- |Richard Scott |Chair of the Scott Trust (1956 – 1984) |- |AP Wadsworth |Chair of the Scott Trust (1948 – 1956) |- |JR Scott |Chair of the Scott Trust (1936 – 1948) |- |Heather Stewart |Journalist director of the Scott Trust Limited board (2011 – 2016) |- |[[Nils Pratley]] |Journalist director of the Scott Trust Limited board (2016 – 2022) |} == The Guardian Foundation == Besides the GMG businesses, the company has a charitable wing: The Guardian Foundation{{EW charity|1153865|THE GUARDIAN FOUNDATION}}{{cite news |title=The Guardian Foundation |url=https://www.theguardian.com/the-guardian-foundation/2016/dec/21/who-we-are-and-what-we-do}} led by Executive Director Rosie Parkyn.{{cite news |title=The Guardian Foundation appoints Rosie Parkyn as its new executive director |url=https://www.theguardian.com/guardian-foundation/2026/jan/07/the-guardian-foundation-appoints-rosie-parkyn-as-executive-director |work=The Guardian |date=7 January 2026}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == * {{Official website|https://www.theguardian.com/about/history}} * [https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/company/06706464/officers Corporate details] from [[Companies House]] {{Guardian Media Group}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:1936 establishments in the United Kingdom]] [[Category:Guardian Media Group]] [[Category:Publishing companies established in 1936]] [[Category:Publishing companies of the United Kingdom]] [[Category:The Guardian]]
